title: Angle Trisection: Minimal Polynomial Degree for Non-Constructibility

problemStatement.plain: It is impossible to trisect a 60° angle using only compass and straightedge, because cos(20°) satisfies an irreducible cubic polynomial over ℚ, and 3 does not divide any power of 2.
whyMatters: One of the three famous classical Greek construction problems
Demonstrates the power of algebraic methods (Wantzel 1837)
Connects geometry to Galois theory and field extensions

proven: The polynomial has no rational roots
3 does not divide any power of 2
Main impossibility for angle trisection, doubling cube, squaring circle

currentState.focus: Improved formalization with proved main theorems
currentState.nextAction: Submit provable variant to Aristotle for the trisection polynomial irreducibility axiom

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETED: Improved formalization from 3 conclusion-axioms to 3 deep axioms + 20 proved theorems. Fixed broken IsConstructible definition. Main impossibility results now proved from axioms rather than axiomatized.
builtItems: Fixed IsConstructible definition (was trivially true, now properly encodes degree condition)
odd_prime_degree_not_constructible: generalized to any odd prime degree
insights: The original IsConstructible def was broken: ∃ n d, d ∣ 2^n ∧ d > 0 is trivially true (d=1, n=0)
Parametrizing IsConstructible by the minpoly degree d makes proofs clean: just show d ∤ 2^n
Three axioms suffice: Wantzel's theorem, polynomial irreducibility, Lindemann's theorem
The no-rational-roots theorem computationally verifies all 8 candidates via norm_num
General framework: any odd prime degree blocks constructibility (odd_prime_not_dvd_power_of_two)
